headline: Automation growth offsets HVAC weakness, margins compress
summary_short: Regal Rexnord's Q1 FY2026 revenue rose to $1,479.1M (+4.3% y/y, -2.9% q/q) as AMC's data-center growth outpaced PES's HVAC decline. Operating income fell to $152.7M (-4.4% y/y) on higher opex, while net income rose 12.2% y/y to $64.3M on a lower tax rate.
summary_long: Revenue grew 4.3% y/y (1.6% organic, 2.7% FX) as AMC (+15.3%, data center/automation strength) and IPS (+5.8%, industrial demand) offset PES's 8.6% decline (residential HVAC weakness). Gross profit rose 4.2% y/y on a $17.2M IPS gain, but opex climbed 8.0% on IPS labor costs and a non-recurring prior-year $6.0M asset-sale gain, pulling operating income down 4.4% y/y and 9.6% q/q. Tax rate fell to 15.9% from 21.2% on a discrete stock-option benefit, lifting net income 12.2% y/y despite lower operating income. Operating cash flow fell $87.4M y/y on working-capital use. Long-term debt fell to $4,682.6M after $1,100M of Senior Notes were refinanced with an $850M term loan; cash fell to $401.0M q/q. FY2026 capex guided to ~$120M.

drivers.explanation: Automation & Motion Control's data-center and discrete-automation strength plus Industrial Powertrain Solutions' general-industrial demand offset Power Efficiency Solutions' residential HVAC weakness; opex growth in IPS compressed operating margin even as a lower tax rate lifted net income.

AMC net sales +15.3% (organic +12.1%) on broad-based growth led by data center and discrete automation, plus food & beverage recovery. IPS +5.8% (organic +2.8%) on general industrial market strength. PES -8.6% (organic -10.3%) on residential HVAC weakness, partly offset by commercial HVAC growth in North America and Asia Pacific.
Increase primarily due to a $17.2 million gain within the IPS segment, driven by higher sales volumes, synergy benefits, and lower restructuring and related costs.
Total operating expenses rose 8.0%, primarily a $19.7 million increase within IPS from higher labor and benefit costs and a $6.0 million gain on asset sale booked in Q1 2025 that did not recur.
Effective tax rate fell to 15.9% from 21.2%, primarily driven by a discrete tax benefit related to stock option exercises in the current year, more than offsetting the decline in operating income.
$87.4 million y/y decrease primarily driven by working capital changes, specifically accounts receivable.

The Company repaid $1,100.0 million of 2026 Senior Notes, funded by $850.0 million in proceeds from the 2025 Term Facility plus $167.8 million of net revolver borrowings, for net debt repayment of $83.5 million in the quarter.
